answer_text:
Let

\[
f'(z)=g(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y).
\]

Since \(f'(z)\) exists on all of \(\mathbb C\), \(f\) is entire, so \(g=f'\) is also entire. Hence \(u\) and \(v\) satisfy the Cauchy–Riemann equations.

We are given

\[
v(x,y)=6x(2y-1)=12xy-6x.
\]

Thus

\[
v_y=12x,\qquad v_x=12y-6.
\]

By the Cauchy–Riemann equations for \(g\),

\[
u_x=v_y=12x,\qquad u_y=-v_x=6-12y.
\]

Integrating \(u_x=12x\) with respect to \(x\),

\[
u(x,y)=6x^2+\phi(y).
\]

Then

\[
u_y=\phi'(y)=6-12y,
\]

so

\[
\phi(y)=6y-6y^2+C,
\]

where \(C\) is a real constant. Therefore

\[
u(x,y)=6x^2-6y^2+6y+C.
\]

Hence

\[
f'(z)=u+iv
=6x^2-6y^2+6y+C+i(12xy-6x).
\]

Writing this in terms of \(z=x+iy\),

\[
6z^2=6x^2-6y^2+12ixy,
\]

and

\[
-6iz=-6i(x+iy)=6y-6ix.
\]

So

\[
f'(z)=6z^2-6iz+C.
\]

Integrating,

\[
f(z)=2z^3-3iz^2+Cz+D.
\]

Using \(f(0)=3-2i\),

\[
D=3-2i.
\]

Using \(f(1)=5-5i\),

\[
f(1)=2-3i+C+3-2i=5-5i+C.
\]

Thus

\[
5-5i+C=5-5i \implies C=0.
\]

Therefore

\[
f(z)=2z^3-3iz^2+3-2i.
\]

Now evaluate at \(z=1+i\). Since

\[
(1+i)^2=2i,
\]

and

\[
(1+i)^3=(1+i)(2i)=-2+2i,
\]

we get

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(1+i)
&=2(-2+2i)-3i(2i)+3-2i \\
&=-4+4i+6+3-2i \\
&=5+2i.
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{5+2i}
\]
